claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

This will help me assess your eligibility for each child individually, as Child Benefit is determined on a per-child basis.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex.

To help me assess whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some information about him.

**How old is Alex, or what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 8 years old.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so he's just in primary school - regular school like any child his age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Alex is in primary school as expected for his age.

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have responsibility for Alex?** For example, do you live with Alex and are you his parent or legal guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives with me. I'm his parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's British.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Thank you for confirming that.

**Are you currently receiving any other benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that answer.

**What is your current annual household income (or approximate income if you're unsure of the exact figure)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly, but it's around average - enough to get by comfortably. Why do you need to know my income?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! I appreciate you asking for clarification.

Income is relevant because Child Benefit has a High Income Child Benefit Charge (HICBC). This means that if your household income is above a certain threshold, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit, but you could face a tax charge on it.

However, I understand you'd prefer not to share exact figures. Let me ask it differently:

**Is your household income above £60,000 per year?**

This will help me understand whether the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not quite sure to be honest. It might be around that mark, but I'd have to check properly. Does that affect whether I can actually claim it though?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! Let me clarify:

**No, it doesn't affect whether you can *claim* Child Benefit.** You would still be eligible to claim it. However, if your income is above £60,000, you may owe a tax charge on the benefit (the High Income Child Benefit Charge), which is something to be aware of.

For the purposes of determining your basic eligibility to claim, what I've gathered so far suggests you would qualify.

Before I provide you with my final assessment, let me ask one more important question:

**Has there been any change in your circumstances since Alex was born - for example, have you ever had your Child Benefit entitlement for Alex stopped or removed, or have you been found ineligible for any reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. I've just never claimed it before - I wasn't sure if I was eligible or how it all worked, so I thought I'd check first.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, let me provide you with my conclusion:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex!**

Here's a summary:

✓ **Alex's age and education**: At 8 years old and in full-time primary education, he meets the age and education requirements.

✓ **Citizenship and residency**: Alex is a British citizen, and you both live in the UK.

✓ **Parental responsibility**: You are his parent with responsibility for him.

✓ **Other circumstances**: You're not receiving income-related benefits that would complicate the claim.

All the key eligibility criteria are met, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

**One reminder**: If your household income is over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge (a tax charge), but this doesn't prevent you from claiming - it's just something to be aware of.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
